title: Purity of the Artin–Schreier sheaf
statement:
Let $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and fix the nondegenerate additive character
$\psi$ of [def-fd-additive-character]. Let $a\in k_0^\times$ and fix
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$ as in
[def-weil-punctual-weights]. The Artin–Schreier sheaf
$\mathcal L_{\psi,ax}$ on $\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$, as defined in
[def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf], is punctually
$\iota$-pure of weight $0$.

proof.text: By [lem-fd-as-lisse], the sheaf $\mathcal L_{\psi,ax}$ is lisse of rank one, so at every closed point $u$ its unique local Frobenius eigenvalue is the trace value $t_{\mathcal L_{\psi,ax}}(u)$ of [lem-fd-as-trace], namely $\psi(\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa(u)/k_0}(au))$. The trace lies in the finite additive group $k_0$, so the homomorphism property of the additive character gives $\psi(\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa(u)/k_0}(au))^{q}=1$; it is therefore a root of unity. By [lem-tw-root-of-unity-modulus], its image under $\iota$ has modulus one. Hence every local eigenvalue $\alpha$ satisfies $|\iota(\alpha)|=1=q_u^{0/2}$, which is precisely punctual $\iota$-purity of weight $0$ by [def-weil-punctual-weights].

The proof is a single audited step using the existing lisse, trace, additive-character, root-of-unity-modulus, and punctual-weight nodes; it also spells out why the trace value is a root of unity.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the sole proof paragraph: lisse rank one identifies the local eigenvalue with the Artin–Schreier trace value, the finite additive-character argument makes it a root of unity, and the modulus calculation gives weight zero.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q140-e8746b831 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both blueprint snapshots (master order 2771 and main-20261015 order 3115, identical), the unit, the chapter and the full statements of every cited node. The delivery has no new nodes. The statement correction (fix psi = Psi∘Tr from def-fd-additive-character and require a in k0^x) is justified: these are exactly the hypotheses of lem-fd-as-trace, and they were undeclared in the source. It drops nothing a citer uses: lem-a1-exceptional-constituents assumes a in k0^x. The single step checks: lem-fd-as-lisse gives rank one, so the eigenvalue equals the trace; lem-fd-as-trace gives the value psi(Tr(au)); psi(t)^q = psi(qt) = psi(0) = 1, so it is a root of unity; lem-tw-root-of-unity-modulus gives |iota| = 1; def-weil-punctual-weights then gives weight 0. Edge cases checked: zero trace, q=2, high-degree points, and p dividing [k0:Fp]. Every cited unit is reached transitively from sk-p-dl-a1-some-weight, so no tool use is needed, and no SGA is cited. No duplicate exists in the DAG. The open Lean entry finiteLowerStar_singleFunctor_of_isAffine is a framework sorry that many reviewed nodes leave unattached the same way, and the item's proof does not use it.
